summary: AI observability has become a critical discipline as LLM deployments scale in complexity and cost, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams operate blind to latency spikes, prompt regressions, runaway token costs, and silent failures in agent pipelines. Gartner predicts that by 2028, LLM observability investments will account for 50% of all GenAI deployments, up from just 15% in early 2026.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, prompt inputs/outputs, token usage, latency, and agent run histories within LangChain and LangGraph ecosystems
features: End-to-end trace visualization for chains and agents
Prompt versioning and management
Dataset creation and regression testing
Human feedback annotation and scoring
Evaluation runs with custom and built-in metrics
Integration with LangChain, LangGraph, and third-party LLMs
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention. Approximately £80/month for 100K requests at scale.
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need deep chain-level tracing, prompt versioning, and built-in evaluation workflows in a tightly integrated ecosystem

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token consumption, cost per request, latency, error rates, and model usage across providers via a proxy gateway layer
features: One-line proxy setup requiring minimal code changes
Real-time cost tracking and spend dashboards by model and user
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and access control per user or API key
Custom properties and metadata tagging on requests
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Open-source and self-hostable
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month with unlimited seats and usage-based overages; Team at $799/month adding SOC-2 and HIPAA; Enterprise custom pricing with SAML SSO and on-prem. Approximately £20/month for 100K requests making it significantly cheaper than LangSmith.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing cost visibility and simplicity who want the fastest setup (under 2 minutes), best-in-class spend tracking, and a lightweight gateway approach without heavy SDK instrumentation

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiment runs, model evaluation metrics, dataset versions, prompt performance, and end-to-end ML pipeline lineage
features: Trace logging for LLM calls, chains, and agents via Weave
Experiment tracking with rich metric visualization
Dataset and artifact versioning for reproducibility
Evaluation framework with custom scorers and leaderboards
Prompt management and comparison across runs
Integration with major LLM providers and ML frameworks
Collaborative dashboards for team review
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50/user/month; Enterprise pricing available on request. Weave tracing is included within W&B subscription tiers.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams already using W&B for experiment tracking who want to extend the same workflow into LLM observability and evaluation without adopting a separate tool

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM span-level traces, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, embedding drift, model performance metrics, latency, error rates, and enterprise-scale telemetry
features: Span-level tracing with OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation
Dashboards for latency, error rates, and token usage
Experiment-style workflows for comparing prompt or model runs
RAG retrieval quality evaluation including relevance scoring
Embedding visualization and drift detection
Online evaluations running continuously in production
Source-available Phoenix for self-hosting; full Arize platform for enterprise
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host. Arize AI managed platform offers a free Developer tier; Growth and Enterprise tiers are usage-based with custom pricing. Enterprise contracts typically start in the tens of thousands annually.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing production-grade telemetry with deep RAG evaluation, embedding monitoring, OpenTelemetry compatibility, and the ability to connect LLM issues to broader ML model performance

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, cost per trace, latency, custom evaluation scores, and user session flows across any LLM provider
features: Detailed LLM tracing with nested span support
Prompt management with versioning and A/B comparison
Custom scoring hooks for human or automated evaluations
Dataset creation from production traces for regression testing
SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and OpenTelemetry integration
Self-hosting option for full data control under MIT license
Strong open-source community with active development
tools.pricing: Langfuse Cloud free for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud tiers start around £20 for 500K requests. Self-hosted is free (open-source) with infrastructure costs estimated around £30/month plus approximately 2 hours of maintenance per month.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a fully open-source, self-hostable tracing and prompt management solution with strong community support, data privacy control, and flexible evaluation hooks without vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token usage, latency, and model interactions via OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation that exports to any observability backend
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK for automatic LLM call instrumentation
Support for major LLM providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and more
Vendor-agnostic design allowing export to Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, or any OTLP backend
Minimal code changes required for integration
Tracing of LangChain, LlamaIndex, and other orchestration frameworks
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
Community-driven with Traceloop maintaining active development
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free. Costs are limited to your chosen observability backend infrastructure or SaaS subscription (e.g., Datadog, New Relic, or self-hosted Grafana stack).
tools.best_for: Teams with an existing OpenTelemetry-based observability stack who want to add LLM monitoring without adopting a dedicated LLM tool, or those prioritizing vendor neutrality and backend flexibility

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, evaluation metrics across 50+ dimensions including hallucination, answer relevancy, faithfulness, bias, toxicity, and RAG pipeline correctness
features: 50+ open-sourced evaluation metrics via the DeepEval framework
Online evaluations running continuously against production traffic
Regression testing suite for catching prompt or model change regressions
Integration with CI/CD pipelines for automated evaluation gates
Datasets and benchmarking for systematic model comparison
Used by teams at OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft
Combines evaluation depth with observability layer integration
tools.pricing: DeepEval open-source framework is free. Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier; Pro and Team tiers with advanced features and higher throughput are available with custom pricing on request.
tools.best_for: Teams for whom output quality and safety evaluation is the primary concern, particularly those building RAG systems or agentic pipelines where hallucination detection and faithfulness scoring are critical requirements

cost_tips: Implement request caching for repeated or semantically similar prompts: tools like Helicone offer built-in caching, and semantic caching libraries can reduce redundant API calls by 20-40% on typical workloads, directly cutting token spend without any quality loss.

Right-size your model selection by routing requests based on task complexity — use smaller, cheaper models such as GPT-4o Mini or Claude Haiku for simple classification or extraction tasks, and reserve frontier models only for tasks that genuinely require their capability, which can reduce costs by 60-80% on mixed workloads.

Monitor and trim prompt token bloat by regularly auditing your system prompts and few-shot examples using tracing tools like Langfuse or LangSmith; verbose or redundant prompt sections often account for 30-50% of input tokens and can be compressed without degrading output quality.

Set hard budget guardrails and rate limits at the API gateway level using tools like Helicone or LangSmith to cap per-user, per-feature, or per-environment spending, combined with alerting on cost anomalies so runaway agent loops or misconfigured retries are caught within minutes rather than at the end of a billing cycle.
